messages:
Maya (Marketing): Pushed a new draft of the battlecard refresh to the doc. Big shift: lead with 'serving' economics not model features. TL;DR — latency SLOs, predictable unit cost, and rollout safety as top rebut hooks. https://redwood.app/drive/battlecard-drafts :eyes:
Omar (Field): Nice. Can we get a one-liner that contrasts with 'cloud AI APIs' specifically around noisy multi-tenant latencies? Sales need something punchy for calls.
Priya (Product): I like calling out 'predictable throughput' + 'automated fallback policies' as the practical win. But add a short caveat line about model parity — "matches quality for most prod use-cases" so we don't overclaim.
Tom (AE): Also need a quick objection handler for procurement: "why not just host on cloud provider endpoints?" — can we include simple cost math? 2 sentences max.
Sam (Research): I added a benchmark summary in the doc — median p95 token latency across our Dedicated vs two major cloud providers on comparable instances. Important: include test harness notes (seq len, batching). Without that folks will misinterpret.
Ruth (Growth): For webinar hooks, consider a 10-min live demo showing fallback in action (region failover -> model variant fallback). It's visual and supports the reliability claim. Could be a good pull for GA signups.
Maya (Marketing): Agree on the demo. For inbound routing, can we tweak the messaging to route people who mention 'cost' -> growth drip, 'SLA' or 'compliance' -> enterprise SDR, 'benchmark' -> technical nurture? I can draft quick routing rules.
Omar (Field): Yes route by intent. Also flag any mention of "private deployment" as high-touch.
Maya (Marketing): Draft routing map pasted below:
```
# simple inbound routing pseudo-rules
if text contains (cost OR price OR savings) -> tag:cost_interest -> growth-nurture
if text contains (sla OR uptime OR compliance OR private) -> tag:enterprise -> assign:enterprise-sdr
if text contains (benchmark OR latency OR p95 OR p99 OR throughput) -> tag:technical -> assign:solutions-eng
```
Tom (AE): Perfect. Can we make the procurement rebuttal line like: "Cloud endpoints are great for early dev — for predictable unit cost and enterprise SLAs, teams choose dedicated inference to avoid tail-latency and noisy neighbors." Short and direct.
Priya (Product): That reads well. Add parenthetical: (we also offer private deployment + KMS for regulated workloads).
Sam (Research): Quick note for the benchmark blurb: include a minimalist table link rather than embedding numbers in the battlecard — numbers will change. Link to running benchmark results with timestamped CSV.
Maya (Marketing): Good call. Ruth — can you own the webinar hook copy and registration CTA? Make it easy for AE follow-up.
Ruth (Growth): On it. I'll draft two CTAs: "See predictable inference in action" (webinar) and "Get a 14-day dedicated trial" (hand-raise).
launch-bot: Reminder: marketing-launch checklist item 3 (battlecard publish) due in 48h.
Omar (Field): I'll shepherd the field-ready one-pager and the 2-up benchmark link. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Maya (Marketing): Thanks team. Next steps: Ruth to draft CTAs + webinar outline by EOD; Sam to attach benchmark link and test notes; Omar to produce one-pager; Priya to review claim caveats; Tom to produce procurement 1-liner. I'll consolidate and publish v1. :thumbsup:
Tom (AE): ack, will send procurement line in 30m.
Priya (Product): I'll slot a 15-min review tomorrow morning. :calendar:
Maya (Marketing): Great — closing thread, will ping when published. :sparkles:
